title: Municipal digital twin
challenge: Inspection and planning teams worked from flat maps and site visits, with no shared spatial picture of the building stock and no way to query it by age or condition.
built: A browser digital twin built on open 3DBAG building data, coloured live by real attributes (construction year, height, roof area) with per-building readouts. Self-hosted, no external tile traffic, works behind a corporate firewall.

title: Defence procedure trainer
challenge: A safety-critical procedure could only be rehearsed on scarce, expensive real equipment, limiting how often crews could train to standard.
built: A VR trainer matching the real procedure step for step, with instructor scenarios, scoring and after-action review. Anonymised by default; nothing site-specific is shown.

title: Clinical device training
challenge: New clinical staff needed confident hands-on competence with a complex device before touching a patient, faster than classroom and shadowing allowed.
built: An immersive device trainer reproducing the interface and workflow, with guided and free-practice modes and objective competency checks.

title: Underground utility guidance
challenge: Field crews excavating near buried cables and pipes relied on paper plans that were hard to relate to the ground in front of them, with real strike risk.
built: An AR overlay registering underground utility records to the real site, so crews see what is beneath them before they dig — readable in daylight and through gloves.

title: On-site assembly guidance
challenge: Complex low-volume assemblies depended on a handful of experts, and errors were caught late, deep into the build.
built: Step-by-step AR work instructions anchored to the part, with inline checks that catch mistakes at the step they happen instead of at final inspection.

title: Grid load simulation
challenge: Planners needed to reason about load and capacity scenarios spatially, but the modelling lived in spreadsheets disconnected from the network's geography.
built: A spatial sandbox that visualises load and capacity scenarios over the network as an honest concept model — a decision aid, kept clearly separate from the real building data in the twin.
